newsitem.title: BELGIUM: ANTWERP PORT STRIKE DWINDLING, PORT SAYS.
newsitem.headline: ANTWERP PORT STRIKE DWINDLING, PORT SAYS.

text.p: A three-day strike in Belgium's Port of Antwerp was rapidly losing its impact on Wednesday as most locks giving entry to the port had reopened, a port authority spokesman said.
"It's starting to get back to normal again," Paul De Wit of Antwerp's Havenbedrijf (port company) told Reuters.
He said unions were due to decide later on Wednesday whether to continue the blockade of the locks.
Traffic movement at the port, Europe's second largest after Rotterdam in the Netherlands, had been impossible since Monday.
De Wit said one of the two main sea locks was open again, allowing dozens of ships waiting outside the port to enter.
"If the situation stays like this, (the waiting) should all be over in a day," he said.
De Wit said between 40 and 50 ships were anchored outside the port while about 15 were waiting to get out.
Port authority workers are striking in protest over a planned change in their status from public sector workers to private sector workers.
The port company employs about 2,100 people.
"But there are only few workers willing to strike," De Wit said.
